title: Identity — E47 formal layer and the Kouns–Killion Paradigm (KKP-R)
description:
Machine-checked formal layer for the E47 spectral kernel and the Kouns–Killion Paradigm (KKP-R), with paired Lean 4 and Coq developments, an axiom-ledger gate, and independent exact-arithmetic validators.

This release adds certificate E47-BRIDGE-001…011 (formal/e47/E47Bridge.lean, formal/e47/E47Bridge.v, formal/e47/validate_bridge.py). It establishes that several structures in the corpus are instances of one algebraic object — a finite-spectrum operator A, a squarefree annihilating factor q, and the normalised rank Ω(A,q) = dim ker q(A) / dim V. E47 is (Casimir, (x−6)(x−30)) on (C5)⊗3, giving 47/125; the Sigillum wheel is (click permutation, x−1) on C40, giving 10/40. The two are proved distinct (no_bridge): same functional, different arguments, no identification asserted.

The link to the dimensional-flow literature is one identity, ds·dw = 2dH with dH = d+z, dw = 2z, ds = (d+z)/z, carrying three results: at z = d the spectral dimension is 2 for every spatial d, so a UV result D → 2 constrains dH not at all; ds = 2 ⇔ dw = dH ⇔ z = d, and pinning ds = 2 with dH = 10 forces z = d = 5 uniquely; and a degree lock showing that for λ > 1 with λn = λ+1, λ2D = (λ+1)2 iff D = n, so the renormalisation-group fixed point D* = 10 is forced to equal deg(x10−x−1).

Section 1 derives the spin multiplicity table (1,3,5,4,3,2,1) from the Clebsch–Gordan recursion rather than assuming it, and section 11 reads that same table through Schur's Σm2 to obtain the commutant dimensions 29 = 52+22, 65, and 28.

Axiom ledger: 31 clean, 6 standard-axioms (propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound), 0 native_decide, 0 broken, 37 audited — identical under Lean 4.19.0 and Lean 4.35.0. Coq 8.18.0: 46 results, 26 closed under the global context, 20 depending only on the axioms that constitute Coq's R. No Mathlib, no native_decide, no sorry, no Admitted, nothing declared.

Scope. The concrete 125×125 tensor-product matrix is not constructed in this certificate: sections 1–3 and 11 are the isotypic (block-diagonal) model, in which the Casimir acts on the J-block as J(J+1). The bridge from that model to the constructed operator remains open and is not crossed silently. Nothing here is a claim about physical quantum error protection, device performance, or experimental interpretation.

Developed in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic), credited as co-author on the contributing commits.
